The exact parent inequality gives ∫(ℓ(Z′)−ℓ(Z))² dπ≤2ℓ_max²R/κ. Thus each edge stays within its level at zero reserve. A positive minimum gap g bounds the mass of unequal-level edges by the stated expression. For any union of whole levels its outgoing minus incoming crossing mass is exactly its Jordan imbalance, so its absolute value is at most all crossing mass.

Restricting to an entire level preserves its Jordan marginals and the physical row mean because all edges stay within their levels. This gives equal mass, full first moments and convex order by affine testing and Jensen, and injectivity assigns one fiber per level.

In the planar single-fiber case a row starting at an extreme point is concentrated there. Mutual singularity of the Jordan marginals forbids positive mass on such identity rows. A nonextreme boundary point is in the relative interior of a maximal supporting segment; its supporting line confines its row to that segment by zero affine slack. The countably many facet endpoints are arclength-null for both marginals. Thus both vanish off the facet interiors, and the restrictions to each facet retain the row mean.

The resulting facet measures have equal mass and tangent first moment, and conditional Jensen for tangent-coordinate hinges gives the nonpositive signed tests in the stated direction from Ξ_+ to Ξ_−. No independent freedom to vary one fiber is used.
